newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank intervenes to halt yuan rise.
newsitem.headline: China central bank intervenes to halt yuan rise.

text.p: China's yuan currency ended unchanged at 8.2900 to the dollar on Wednesday as the central bank intervened to keep the currency from breaching the key psychological level, dealers said.
They said banks tried to push the currency above the 8.2900 level but selling, believed to be from the People's Bank of China, emerged to halt any advance.
Dealers had seen a more relaxed stance by the central bank towards the currency's strength, particularly out of concern that it not allow recent weakness of other Asian currencies to affect the yuan.
But the central bank, despite its concerns over currency speculation elsewhere in Asia, apparently did not want the currency to push through the psychological barrier just yet.

"The 8.2900 level is a very important psychological point," said another dealer. "If it is breached, the yuan will rise sharply. So the central bank intervened to depress the yuan as soon as it tested that level."
Other dealers agreed with that assessment but they added the trading level may still be breached before too long.
"The central bank prefers a steady movement of the yuan, which it thinks is beneficial to China's economy," another dealer said.
"But if fundamentals continue to support the yuan, it will be hard for the central bank to keep it below the 8.2900 level over the longer term," the dealer said.

The yuan briefly hit a high of 8.2899 but it traded between 8.2902/8.2905 for most of the session. It opened at 8.2900 and hit a low of 8.2945 during a brief bout of speculative selling with the weighted average price on Tuesday at 8.2903.

Dealers said they expected the yuan to hold steady near 8.2900 on Thursday. The yuan closed up at 7.0083 from 7.0526 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intraday high of 1.0696 from 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar.
